findings.title: Unary operand precedence
findings.message: Unary +/- parses its operand with min precedence 3, so the operand loop never consumes binary operators. That is correct for precedence, but unary minus applied to a unit-less scalar then multiplied works; however '-2 mm' yields a.n negated before unit scaling only in the inner parse, fine. The real risk: ParseFloat of tokens like '1e999' returns an error with ±Inf, so ok. No issue beyond unary precedence making '-2*3' parse as (-2)*3, acceptable.
findings.suggestion: Verify tests cover unary operators with higher-precedence operands.

findings.title: Units only accepted directly after number literals
findings.message: After p.next() consumes the number, TokenText is read for the unit. But the unit branch is inside a path where a number followed by a variable name (e.g. '2 width') is rejected as unknown unit. More importantly, a unit token directly after a parenthesized expression, such as '(1+2) mm', fails with 'invalid expression suffix'. Also, a variable name used as an identifier sets dimension=1 even though it is a plain length in mm, which is fine, but 'unknown' identifiers in the Ident case are not bounded by the token budget check order.
findings.suggestion: Support unit suffixes on parenthesized groups, or document that units only apply to numeric literals; add tests such as '(1+2) mm'.

finding.title: Move target not validated against disabled items
finding.message: The FeatureTimeline test disables Items[0] then calls Activate on the 'later' button, expecting no change. propose only checks the Disabled flag on the item being moved, but the move target index is not checked for a disabled neighbor, and also a rollback marker button isn't blocked by p.Disabled at view level for the root Node only. Additionally propose's found loop finds the last matching ID without break, harmless since IDs are unique.
finding.suggestion: Decide whether moving past disabled items is allowed and validate the target accordingly.
